knowledge_graph.title: Eating disorder
knowledge_graph.description: An eating disorder is a mental disorder defined by abnormal eating behaviors that adversely affect a person's physical or mental health. These behaviors may include eating too much food or too little food, as well as body image issues.

related_questions.question: What is the meaning of eating disorder?
related_questions.snippet: Eating disorders are serious illnesses marked by severe disturbances in a person's eating behaviors. Although many people may be concerned about their health, weight, or appearance on occasion, some become fixated or obsessed with weight loss, body weight or shape, and controlling their food intake.
related_questions.title: Eating Disorders - National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH)

related_questions.question: What is an eating disorder best described as?
related_questions.snippet: An eating disorder is a mental health condition where you use the control of food to cope with feelings and other situations. Unhealthy eating behaviours may include eating too much or too little or worrying about your weight or body shape.
related_questions.title: Overview – Eating disorders - NHS

related_questions.question: What qualifies as disordered eating?
related_questions.snippet: Disordered eating may include restrictive eating, compulsive eating, or irregular or inflexible eating patterns. Dieting is one of the most common forms of disordered eating. Australian adolescents engaging in dieting are five times more likely to develop an eating disorder than those who do not diet (1).
related_questions.title: Disordered Eating & Dieting - National Eating Disorders Collaboration

related_questions.question: How do you treat eating disorder?
related_questions.snippet: It usually includes a mix of specific types of talk therapy, also known as psychotherapy, as well as medical monitoring and sometimes nutrition education or medicines. Eating disorder treatment also involves taking care of other medical problems that an eating disorder causes or makes worse.
